audit.why: TRICKY 7/10 fits: 52.83% WR over 4800 games, early lane is Syndra's on range but level 6 roam/all-in threat is genuine and side lane is dangerous.
Spikes are right: Syndra owns 1-5, level 6 is the coin-flip (Shadow Assault + E-wall roam), first item restores one-shot threat, late Talon is a flank assassin.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart sides (Talon rows 0-3, Skill rows 4 and 6) contradicted the content win[] layer, the packet chart, and the whys under them — phases[0].why says 'best poke in the mage pool' while the row said Talon wins. Cooldowns field had no digit; two bullets were tradeGood/tradeBad pasted verbatim.
audit.why: Talon's Q leap is 575 range on an 8s cooldown and Rake 9s>7s is his only ranged damage — Syndra's 800-range Q and held E beat that pattern pre-6, which is what every prose field already said.
audit.corrected: Chart rows 0-4 and 6 moved to agree with win[] and packet (Syndra, with 5 staying Skill... row 5 already agreed); whys rewritten to Talon-specific facts; cooldowns rewritten with 9s/7s Rake, 8s Q, 15s E numbers.

edits.before: Q on every last-hit he takes — your level 1 poke is the best in the mage pool. Leave spheres on the ground; they're ammo.
edits.after: Talon is melee at 1 — Q taxes every last-hit he walks up for, and spheres left on the ground are stun ammo for later.

edits.before: Q-E already threatens the stun — most mids don't respect it at 2 and pay a Flash for the lesson.
edits.after: Q-E already threatens the stun, and Rake alone cannot win a poke war against your 800 range.

edits.before: Full kit: W-slow into QE stun into Q again is a half-bar rotation. The lane is yours to bully from here.
edits.after: Full kit: hold E for his Q leap — stun him mid-jump and his all-in becomes a free half-bar trade for you.

edits.before: Splinter stacks build toward empowered Q — keep poking; every sphere thrown is scaling AND pressure at once.
edits.after: Rake at 9s is his only ranged poke — chip in its downtime and bank spheres; he has no answer at range.

edits.before: Unleashed Power online — count spheres before every trade: three-plus on the field means most mids die to R alone.
edits.after: Both ults arrive at 6, but a QE stun the instant he surfaces from Shadow Assault flips his all-in into your kill.

edits.before: Late Syndra is a one-button court-martial: flank, QE the carry, R the verdict. Spheres on the ground are sentences waiting.
edits.after: You out-pick the honest 5v5 — QE the flank the instant he surfaces and R finishes; only a caught-alone Syndra loses here.

edits.before: Level 6 is skill-dependent: his R roam threat is real but a clean QE stun on his surface neutralizes it.
edits.after: Level 6 leans yours: his R all-in is real, but a clean QE stun the moment he surfaces neutralizes it.

edits.before: - Talon Rake: matchup-defining — The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your E Scatter the Weak like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Rake is 9s at rank 1, 7s maxed, and the return line is most of his damage — trade in the gap after it misses. - His Q leap is 8s: stun the jump and he has nothing for eight more. - Your E is 15s; guard it like a fifth summoner. - R only for kill windows.

edits.before: The boomerang return is most of his lane damage — stand off the return line. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Spheres pre-banked make QE instant — his Q leap closes in a blink, and a stun you must set up first arrives too late.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, W-slow the dodge attempt, QE the slowed line, Q again — a full bar of damage that started as routine poke.
edits.after: His Q leap is only 575 range and telegraphed — with E in hand the jump lands into an instant stun and the all-in dies with him.

edits.before: Spending E on chip-spacing and then watching the dash you bought it for arrive unanswered — the stun is the matchup, not the damage.
edits.after: Your E is 15 seconds — chasing a half-HP Talon without it hands him a free W-Q turnaround; he only needs one clean combo to flip it.

edits.before: No permanent owner here — the level chart shows where momentum tilts and tilts back.
edits.after: The chart leans Syndra at nearly every stage — only the first-item window is a genuine coin-flip.

notes: Chart repair: full sides rows 0-4 and 6 moved to Syndra; content win[] already held Syndra on those rows and packet levelChart agrees (row 5 Skill agrees on all three layers), so no win[] edits were needed — side/rating/why moved as one group. whys[4] content was rewritten because it said 'skill-dependent' under a Syndra verdict. Templated-but-unfixed: ahead, breakdown.carry, breakdown.feeding, breakdown.mid remain generic Syndra prose; nothing Talon-specific verifiable to swap in without inventing. Talon's W flag says knockup — Riot's description mentions no displacement; trusted the description and did not write any knockup claim.
